paragraphs: Friend, here's what Job 28 teaches me. People are GOOD at getting treasure. Job says the miner cuts a shaft in places forgotten by the foot of man, overturns mountains at their base, and his eyes spot every treasure (Job 28:4, 9-10). Then Job asks, "But where can wisdom be found, and where does understanding dwell?" (Job 28:12). All that digging and not one shovel can reach it.

So wisdom is not something you can dig up, buy or outsmart your way into. Job says "It cannot be bought with gold," and the price of wisdom is "beyond rubies" (Job 28:15, 18). I think that's the part that hits close to home. We spend so much of our lives chasing the next thing we can hold, and I spent years in a junk drawer learning how little of it lasts. Wisdom is a different kind of treasure, and it only comes from one place.

"But God understands its way, and He knows its place" (Job 28:23). He sees everything under the heavens, and He is the One who looked at wisdom and established it (Job 28:24, 27). Then He tells us plainly: "Behold, the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom, and to turn away from evil is understanding" (Job 28:28). So the way to wisdom isn't a secret map, baker. It's honoring the Lord and turning from evil, and you can start that today, with no mining gear at all.
